findings.claim: The per-row power-of-two quotient specialisation in #422 does not reach the named Foundry consumer. #422's Rust changes are confined to the `u64x64` example target, which no crate can depend on. The consumer's executable G1 and G6 paths evaluate no per-row stock quotient: they compare stock against a precomputed `d * q`.

findings.claim: The executable path does evaluate integer division: `(q + per_staff - 1) / per_staff`. It is the threshold operand of a mask predicate and names no lane, so it is computed once when the predicate is built, not per row. A per-row quotient specialisation has nothing to apply to.
